name: Quan Dui
description: Quan Dui (Quán Duì 全對) means "complete pairs". It is a simple Rummy-like draw-and-discard game played with Chinese money cards (Dongguan Pai). The object is to collect a 16-card hand of eight pairs; identical pairs (dui) or same-number different-suit pairs (ka). Played in Dongguan, Guangdong, China; observed in Chinese clubs abroad.

rules.objective: Collect a 16-card hand consisting of eight pairs. Win the agreed stake from each other player; if all eight pairs are dui (identical cards), win double stake (quan dui).
rules.gameplay: Dealer gets 16 cards, others 15 each; stock is face-down. Play is anticlockwise. Each turn: optionally take the top discard (to complete a pair or win) or draw from stock; then discard one card face-up. Only the most recent discard is available. Priority for taking discard: (1) completing eight pairs to win, (2) forming dui (identical pair), (3) player to discarder's right. First to expose eight pairs wins; winner deals next hand.
keyRules: Dui: pair of identical cards. Ka: pair of same number, different suits (odd cards count as ones).
If two want the same discard for dui, the player nearer to discarder's right has priority. Completing a hand beats claiming for dui.
Optional: with eight mixed ka/dui pairs you may keep playing for quan dui (all dui) for double stake, unless you claimed a discard to make your final ka.
